meta.source: Emotional-content strategy research — recurring visual styles & high-demand mental-wellness angles, compiled 2026-08-06
meta.core_principle: Generic affirmations underperform. The strongest posts name a specific, articulable felt experience the viewer has had but may not have put words to. Every caption's opening line should create self-recognition, permission, or a productive contradiction — never a vague affirmation.
meta.visual_principle: Avoid making every image purely serene. The strongest visuals open with visible tension (a closed door, a divided reflection, floating obligations, an empty chair) and resolve it by the final impression. Resolution, not just calm, is the payoff.
meta.compliance_note: Every hook, visual concept, and caption drawn from this file still must pass the Meta/Instagram compliance rules already defined in each trigger routine — no medical claims, no diagnosing the reader, no 'cures'/'heals'/'permanently resets' language, no fabricated statistics or testimonials. Nervous-system and grief content is a supportive practice, never a treatment or cure. If a hook below reads as clinical or absolute, soften it in the actual caption (e.g. 'may help your body settle' rather than 'resets your nervous system').

hook_templates: You do not have to ___ before you…
This is what ___ can look like.
You can be grateful and still…
Your body may be telling you…
If you have been feeling ___, this may be why.
The strongest version of you may need…

face_led_authority.description: A single trusted presenter speaks directly to camera or appears in a tightly-edited interview-style clip. Credibility comes from the face; captions carry the message without sound.
face_led_authority.ai_adaptation: Use a consistent, natural-looking digital presenter. Avoid over-polished skin, artificial gestures, or futuristic backgrounds that read as manufactured.

minimal_editorial_quote.description: One emotionally resonant sentence over paper textures, muted backgrounds, book pages, or restrained lifestyle footage — reflective, 'choose yourself' style posts.
minimal_editorial_quote.ai_adaptation: Cream paper, subtle film grain, serif typography, slow shadows, window light, handwritten accents, one symbolic object.

cinematic_emotional_metaphor.description: Rather than literally depicting an emotion, the image visualizes the internal experience: hesitation at a doorway, carrying invisible weight, smiling while exhausted, surrounded by unfinished obligations.
cinematic_emotional_metaphor.ai_adaptation: Create visually impossible but emotionally recognizable scenes — this is where generative imagery outperforms ordinary stock photography.

candid_vulnerability.description: Unscripted-feeling disclosures about panic, grief, body commentary, loneliness, overwhelm.
candid_vulnerability.ai_adaptation: Never fabricate a fake personal testimony. Use narrated composite stories, clearly framed reflections, or symbolic first-person storytelling only.

what_it_looks_like_vs_feels_like.description: Split between the competent, composed external image and the overloaded internal one — especially effective for high-functioning anxiety, burnout, grief, people-pleasing.
what_it_looks_like_vs_feels_like.ai_adaptation: Split screens, mirrored characters, transparent layers, double exposure, or a polished exterior paired with a chaotic shadow world.

anxiety_begin_before_ready.title: Anxiety: Begin Before You Feel Ready
anxiety_begin_before_ready.core_promise: You can move while uncertainty is still present — you do not have to wait for fear to disappear before you act.
hooks: You do not have to feel fearless before you move.
Anxiety grows in the space between knowing and beginning.
Waiting to feel ready may be what keeps you stuck.
Your next step does not require your fear's permission.
anxiety_begin_before_ready.visual_concept: A sophisticated woman, approximately 40-55, stands before a glowing doorway. Her shadow remains frozen behind her while her physical body steps forward into light. Papers labeled 'What if?' dissolve into light around her.

high_functioning_burnout.title: High-Functioning Burnout: The Hidden Cost of Being Strong
high_functioning_burnout.core_promise: Exhaustion is not evidence of inadequacy; it may be evidence of prolonged over-functioning.
hooks: Burnout does not always look like falling apart.
Sometimes burnout looks like being dependable for too long.
You are not lazy. You have been carrying too much.
Rest may not work when the life exhausting you remains unchanged.
high_functioning_burnout.visual_concept: A professionally dressed woman sits calmly at a desk while dozens of translucent calendars, notifications, family responsibilities, and emotional demands orbit around her. With each breath, the objects gently fall away.
best_formats: what people see / what I feel split screen
diagnostic-style carousel: 'Quiet Signs You Are Carrying Too Much'

boundaries_and_outgrowing.title: Boundaries, Healthy Love, and Outgrowing Access
boundaries_and_outgrowing.core_promise: Healing changes the relationships, behaviors, and environments you can continue tolerating.
hooks: Healing changes who still has access to you.
Not everyone who knew the old you can accompany the healed you.
A boundary is not revenge. It is clarity.
You can love someone and still close the door.
Outgrowing a relationship does not erase what it once meant.
boundaries_and_outgrowing.visual_concept: A woman walks through an archway into a blooming garden. Behind her is a dim room filled with old photographs and open doors. She does not destroy the past; she simply closes the gate gently.
best_formats: symbolic still with a strong caption

body_first_nervous_system.title: Body-First Healing and Nervous-System Micro-Resets
body_first_nervous_system.core_promise: Sometimes the body needs evidence of safety before the mind can receive another affirmation.
hooks: Your mind may not be where healing begins.
You cannot always think your way out of a body that feels unsafe.
Before you solve the problem, help your body leave emergency mode.
Try this when your thoughts are moving faster than your breath.
body_first_nervous_system.visual_concept: A luminous wave travels from the woman's feet through her chest and into her brain. A chaotic red-gold energy field gradually becomes soft sage and rose-colored light as she breathes.
body_first_nervous_system.compliance_flag: Present as a supportive practice only. Never claim a breathing exercise heals trauma or permanently resets the nervous system.

emotional_duality.title: "I Am Fine" Stories: Grief, Panic, and Emotional Duality
emotional_duality.core_promise: Conflicting emotions do not make you ungrateful, weak, or broken.
hooks: You can be grateful and grieving at the same time.
A beautiful life can still contain painful days.
Sometimes 'I'm fine' means 'I do not know where to begin.'
Healing does not require you to stop missing what was lost.
Strength and sadness can live in the same body.
emotional_duality.visual_concept: A woman holds two bouquets: one blooming and one releasing petals. Sunlight falls on one side of her face while gentle rain falls on the other. The visual communicates integration, not despair.

pilot_series.title: What Strength Really Looks Like
pilot_series.note: Available as an optional 5-episode limited run (e.g. mapped across one week's slots) if a dedicated push is wanted later. Not wired into the daily rotation by default.
episodes: Strength can look like asking for help.
Strength can look like disappointing someone.
Strength can look like resting before the breakdown.
Strength can look like grieving without explaining yourself.
Strength can look like beginning while still afraid.
